input.task: What is the main heading on this page?

expect.note: rows 1-2 are the two ways of not specifying a model (absent, explicit null) and must both default; row 3 is the default by explicit name (allowlisted, NOT ablated); rows 4-7 are the four ablation ids

provenance: the other half of the allowlist, and the half an outside observer cannot see. A `model` field that is accepted and then dropped on the floor returns exactly the same 200 and the same run_id as one that works, so the M9 ablation would have run four times against the default model and produced a tradeoff table in which every row was the same model wearing four names — an artifact indistinguishable from a real measurement and completely false. Watched red before any of it existed: the field was not on `TaskIn` and `_execute` called `live_planner()` with no argument, so all five rows returned 200 and the recorder captured `null` — not the wrong model, no model at all. Row 1 was red for the same reason and had to be, since 'the default still reaches the planner' is the thing the other four are measured against. Re-watched red at the owner's model-set change (2026-08-20): with the endpoint still gating on ABLATION_MODELS, the four new ids reached the planner but row 2 — the incumbent default named explicitly — came back 422 with planner_model null, because the one list was doing both jobs and the default had just been priced out of the ablation set. That is the whole reason ALLOWED_MODELS and ABLATION_MODELS are now separate. Row 2 added in review round 1 (PR #15, R8): posting `{"model": null}` returns 200 and the planner receives the default, which is sane but was not what ADR-010 Decision 7 said ('only an ABSENT field falls back'). Reproduced, then the rule was written to match the behaviour rather than the behaviour bent to match the rule — JSON null is the absent value for an optional field. The row exists so whichever way it is decided, it is decided once and stays decided.

triage.note: tagged invariant for the same reason as the refusal half: this is what makes the ablation's independent variable actually independent, and it is unobservable from the HTTP response. Row 1 pins the no-model default so M9 cannot change the default model as a side effect (ADR-010 Decision 6 — the default is unchanged in this PR because no data exists yet). `verified_ids_file` pins `planner.ALLOWED_MODELS` — order included — against the frozen snapshot of the OpenRouter response it was verified from, so editing either list without re-verifying is a red case rather than a stale ADR sentence. `price_ceiling` grades the owner's constraint itself: every ablated model must be at or under `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`'s list price on BOTH prompt and completion, and the incumbent default must be OVER it — the second half is what makes ADR-010's 'no cell measures the incumbent' a graded fact rather than a sentence that can go stale when prices move.

provenance_2026_08_21: Three rows moved when the ablation's data arrived (ADR-010 Decision 16). The two default rows (absent `model`, explicit null) now expect `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`: every candidate tied on correctness, so Decision 5's pre-committed rule fell to its cost tie-breaker and this is the cheapest cell. The third row is the interesting one — it used to assert that `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` stayed reachable by explicit name while being priced out of the comparison, and it now asserts the opposite, a 422. Once the ablation picked a replacement, an allowlist that still accepted the superseded incumbent would leave a public endpoint able to spend on the model this system deliberately stopped paying for. The id is kept in the frozen snapshot, and the adapter now requires it to stay there and to stay over the ceiling: Decision 6 excluded it on price, and an exclusion nothing re-checks is a claim, not a guard.
provenance_2026_08_30: Owner revoked ADR-027's loop-mode price exception after an unexpected $33 Opus 5 charge. Every accepted model is now swept against the frozen DeepSeek V4 Pro ceiling. DeepSeek V4 Pro is the default, GPT-5 mini the fallback, and Opus 5 must be refused in every mode. The access_gate conjunct also drives missing/wrong/right/unconfigured credentials through the real HTTP boundary and proves invalid requests allocate no run or model. Watched red against the old state: the two defaults were Luna, GPT-5 mini was refused, Opus was accepted, the all-allowed ceiling sweep reported Opus above both caps, every /tasks credential row returned 200, and /access/verify was 404.
provenance_m51_2026_08_30: M51 narrows public canonical overrides to the two policy routes: explicit DeepSeek V4 Pro pins Pro, explicit GPT-5 mini pins Mini, and historic ablation-only IDs are rejected rather than accepted and silently rerouted through Pro→Mini.
provenance_access_length_2026_08_30: Owner requires a 10-character demo key. The access-gate conjunct now pins the exact boundary: a configured 10-character value verifies and reaches the planner, while a configured 9-character value is refused even when presented exactly. Watched red first with the old 16-character minimum: the right-key verification and task both returned 401.
